summary: Jada Pinkett Smith explained in a Parade interview about her memoir Worthy that she and Will Smith skipped a prenup when they married in 1997 because they promised divorce wouldn't be necessary. She also said they have lived "completely separate lives" for seven years but remain committed to a "life partnership." The article collects related remarks from Jada and Will across several interviews and shows.
one_line: Jada Pinkett Smith says she and Will Smith skipped a prenup in 1997 because they promised never to divorce, despite living separately for seven years.
key_facts: Jada Pinkett Smith, 52, told Parade while discussing her memoir Worthy that she and Will Smith did not sign a prenup when they married in 1997.
Jada said the promise to figure things out was made while "sitting on a log in his mother's backyard," without the "bridal wedding beauty."
In a Today interview with Hoda Kotb aired 13 October, Jada said she and Will have been living "completely separate lives" for the past seven years.
Jada said of divorce: "I made a promise that there will never be a reason for us to get a divorce."
Asked why they didn't "just amicably divorce," Jada replied: "We don't want to."
Jada and Will share two children, Jaden, 25, and Willow, 22; Will also has a 30-year-old son, Trey, with ex-wife Sheree Zampino.
On a 2018 episode of Red Table Talk on Facebook Watch, Jada said she is "not mature enough to have a divorce."
Will Smith said on the Ellen Degeneres Show that "divorce just can't be an option" for him and Jada, and that they "removed the other options."
Jada told People that she and Will had been separated for six years at the time of the 2022 Academy Awards, when Will slapped Chris Rock.
On 16 October Will told the New York Times that Jada's memoir "kind of woke him up" and that she is more "resilient, clever and compassionate than he'd understood."
Jada said of her children: "They're little gurus. They've taught me a deep sense of self-acceptance."
